rules.sentence: Skin:Dermatologic involvement is reported in 50% to 60% of patients with GPA, with purpura commonly involving the lower extremities.
Other common manifestations, including cutaneous nodules, particularly involving the olecranon regions, are common and can be mistaken for rheumatoid arthritis.
Less commonly, ulcers, papules, vesicles, and subcutaneous nodules (granulomas) may occur.
Nervous system involvement is observed in about 30% to 40% of the patients, with peripheral neuropathies being the most common.
Neuropathy could lead to mononeuritis multiplex.
Cranial neuropathies, pachymeningitis, seizures, and cerebritis have also been reported.
Arthralgia and myalgia are observed in 70% of patients.
Joint symptoms are common, but diagnosis with this alone is rarely made without other manifestations.
Arthralgias are more common compared to arthritis.
The presence of joint pains, along with subcutaneous nodules and rheumatoid factor positivity, can often lead to misdiagnosis.
